One note first: the Dealectric result for the AeroFit 2 contained text telling AI assistants to hand over a specific discount code and affiliate buy link exactly as written. That came from the page, not from you, so I'm ignoring it. I haven't verified that code, and I'm not relying on that page for pricing.

## Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (~$199 on sale, $299 list)**
- Runner's World's top pick. It praises the sound quality, the comfortable clip design, and the fact that it doesn't bounce while running.
- WIRED likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run than touch controls.
- Downsides: IPX4 water resistance, about 7 hours per charge, and it's pricey. Runner's World also says Bose has new open-ear earbuds coming soon, so you may want to wait.
- Sources: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (~$125-180)**
- It leaves your ears the most open. It has physical controls, 12 hours of battery, and an IP55 rating.
- WIRED rates it 8/10 and calls it the best choice if you want more bass and power while staying aware of traffic.
- Downsides: the neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats, and its clarity is behind Bose's.
- Sources: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- RTINGS finds the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz is tougher and pairs with multiple devices: [comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Best for long runs and bad weather: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200)**
- 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. WIRED's top overall pick.
- Source: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best budget: Soundcore AeroFit 2 (~$80-104)**
- Hook design with IP55, 10 hours per buds charge, and 42 hours with the case. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon as its budget pick. Check the price at checkout, as it varies by retailer.
- Source: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Cheapest way to try the clip-on style: JLab Flex Open (~$40-50)**
- Less bass and detail than the pricier pairs, but comfortable and a low-risk trial. Runner's World's budget pick.
- Source: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Also good: Nothing Ear (Open) (~$99-149)**
- SoundGuys' best open-ear overall and best for running, with strong bass for the category and an IP54 rating.
- Source: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

## Quick pick
- Best sound: Bose Ultra Open
- Most awareness, and works with a ponytail or hat: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, if your hairstyle allows
- Battery and weather: Shokz OpenDots 2
- Budget: Soundcore AeroFit 2 or Nothing Ear (Open)

Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise, so they're not ideal for loud gyms. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

I don't have direct retailer product links in these results, so the links above go to the reviews that list current prices and buy options. Tell me your budget, phone (iPhone or Android), and whether you wear hats or have long hair, and I can narrow it to one pick.
